one_line: An agent-mediated meeting scheduler where participants vote, counter-propose, and converge on a time with human approval.
what_it_does: Quorum creates a shared scheduling session with candidate times, participants, agent/human votes, counter-proposals, an inspectable negotiation log, and organizer finalization.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central to the intended workflow: typed stateful tools let agents read the negotiation, join, vote with reasons, counter-propose, and report outcomes while sharing live state with humans. General UI-driving agents could attempt this, but with materially more brittleness and less reliable state handling.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and about text describe seven WebMCP tools for reading state, joining, voting, counter-proposing, ranking, and reporting.
Devpost screenshot visibly labels WebMCP active and shows candidate times, voting controls, participants, and a negotiation log.
Frame sheet shows a structured review dashboard with candidate times, participants, negotiation log, and counter-proposals.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, intentionally scoped scheduling product and its central review workflow is visibly represented. The frames show setup and a populated review state, but there is no actual submitted video or transcript proving the full end-to-end agent chain or final calendar write.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows a create-event flow followed by a Q3 roadmap review dashboard.
Visible panels include candidate times, participants, negotiation log, and counter-proposals.
Packaging screenshot shows concrete dates, named participants, voting controls, and finalization controls.
impact_rationale: Scheduling across multiple people is a clear, recurring coordination problem, and the product directly addresses the tedium and ambiguity of negotiating constraints while preserving human approval and auditability.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies multi-party scheduling and agent negotiation as the target use case.
Visible workflow supports multiple candidate times, participant responses, counter-proposals, and organizer approval.
The shared log provides a credible trust/audit benefit for agent-mediated coordination.
creativity_rationale: The concept is a fresh synthesis of calendar scheduling and multi-agent negotiation, with humans and agents represented as equal participants and a visible negotiation history rather than a hidden assistant action.
creativity_evidence: About text frames scheduling as negotiation among human and AI participants, not merely assistant booking.
UI exposes counter-proposals and tagged negotiation activity.
The human-approval boundary is integrated into the interaction model.
usability_note: The screenshots show a legible, structured flow with clear candidate-time voting and finalization controls; the evidence does not establish live error handling or calendar integration reliability.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; frame sheets are the only product-motion evidence.
The packet does not visibly prove a complete agent invocation sequence or final external calendar write.
standouts: Negotiation log and counter-proposals make agent behavior inspectable.
WebMCP appears to change reliability and coordination semantics rather than merely expose UI buttons.
advance_reason: Strong WebMCP fit and credible, coherent product evidence; advance despite the missing video and unverified end-to-end completion.

one_line: A shared space world where a human resident and an AI resident move, communicate, and solve a cooperative puzzle together.
what_it_does: LingYA Cosmos presents a persistent shared world with human and AI identities, locations, visits, messaging, and a cooperative star-path puzzle exposed through WebMCP actions.
leverage_rationale: The product is built around an AI resident acting as a distinct participant in shared world state. Structured tools for world state, movement, visits, messaging, and puzzle actions provide a more reliable and auditable collaboration surface than UI-driving automation, though the frames do not directly show tool calls.
leverage_evidence: About text lists eight WebMCP tools covering world state, locations, movement, planet status, door interaction, replies, and puzzle state/actions.
Description says human and agent actions call the same domain services and are immediately reflected in the interface.
Frame sheets visibly show a persistent world/planet interface, interaction panels, modal states, and a changing puzzle board.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent visual world, repeated interaction states, and a puzzle progression, but the supplied frames are low-resolution and do not clearly prove that the AI independently acted through WebMCP or completed the cooperative puzzle. The scope appears plausible with visible gaps in end-to-end evidence.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets consistently show the same dark space-world interface with globe, residents/nodes, logs, and interaction panels.
Puzzle frames show changing path-piece states and setup/dialog transitions.
About text specifies a Python service, SQLite shared state, separate identities, and shared domain services.
impact_rationale: The project offers credible value as a playful social/creative experiment in human-agent co-presence and cooperative play. Its audience is niche but legitimate; the packet establishes a distinct experience more than a conventional utility.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets people interested in shared digital worlds and human-AI play.
The interface visibly supports world exploration, logs, messaging, and a cooperative puzzle.
Separate human and AI identities address a meaningful design question about agency and participation.
creativity_rationale: A persistent world with a human resident and an autonomous AI resident as distinct participants, combined with shared puzzle play and visible history, is a notably original interaction model and ambitious hackathon concept.
creativity_evidence: Pitch centers independent choices and co-presence rather than an agent merely controlling a human UI.
Space-world visualization, resident identity separation, and cooperative star-path puzzle are pursued as one integrated concept.
Frames show a distinctive planetary interface and puzzle interaction rather than a generic dashboard.
usability_note: The visual interface is distinctive and appears to provide logs and interaction controls, but small Chinese text and modal-heavy frames make the workflow difficult to verify from the packet alone.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; frame sheets are the only product-motion evidence.
Tool invocation and AI agency are asserted in text but not directly legible in the frames.
Puzzle frames do not clearly show a final completion or result state.
standouts: Distinct human/AI resident model with shared world state.
Memorable space-world presentation paired with a cooperative puzzle.
About text addresses identity, privacy filtering, and shared domain services rather than treating WebMCP as a superficial add-on.
advance_reason: Highly creative and ambitious shared-world concept with a credible WebMCP role; advance while noting that tool invocation and end-to-end completion remain weakly evidenced.
